subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which remnant is left when the core of an extremely massive star collapses so much that not even light can escape?
questions.explain: If the collapsing core after a supernova is massive enough, it forms a black hole, whose gravity is so strong that not even light can escape. Less massive cores leave a neutron star.

questions.q: Why should people limit their exposure to ultraviolet radiation from the Sun or sunbeds?
options: UV cools the skin too much
UV is ionising and can damage skin cells, causing sunburn and increasing skin cancer risk
questions.explain: Ultraviolet is ionising enough to damage skin cells and DNA, leading to sunburn, premature ageing and an increased risk of skin cancer; sunscreen and limiting exposure reduce the risk.

questions.q: What is observed in the light from distant galaxies?
questions.explain: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted — its wavelength is increased (shifted towards the red end). This shows the galaxies are moving away from us.

questions.q: A converging (convex) lens is used as a magnifying glass. What type of image does it form when the object is closer than the focal length?
options: Real, upright and the same size
questions.explain: When the object is within the focal length of a converging lens, the lens acts as a magnifying glass, producing a virtual, upright, magnified image on the same side as the object.

questions.q: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: Within the visible spectrum, red light has the longest wavelength and lowest frequency, while violet has the shortest wavelength and highest frequency.

questions.q: Which EM wave is used to take images of broken bones and is ionising?
questions.explain: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone, producing medical images. They are ionising, so exposure is kept as low as possible.

questions.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a star?
options: A nebula (cloud of dust and gas) collapsing into a protostar
questions.explain: A star begins as a nebula. Gravity pulls the dust and gas together to form a protostar, which heats up until nuclear fusion of hydrogen begins, forming a main sequence star.

questions.q: A perfect black body is best described as an object that:
options: Absorbs all the radiation that hits it and is also the best possible emitter
Reflects all radiation that hits it
questions.explain: A perfect black body absorbs all radiation incident on it and is also the best possible emitter of radiation. All bodies emit and absorb infrared (and other) radiation.

questions.q: Compared with radio waves, gamma rays have a:
questions.explain: Gamma rays sit at the high-frequency end of the spectrum, so they have a much shorter wavelength and higher frequency than radio waves (frequency and wavelength are inversely related for a fixed speed).

questions.q: Total internal reflection is used to carry light along optical fibres. Which other application relies on it?
options: An endoscope used to see inside the body
questions.explain: Endoscopes and optical fibres use total internal reflection to guide light (and images) along curved fibres without it escaping the sides.

questions.q: When a nucleus emits a beta-minus particle, how does its atomic number change?
questions.explain: In beta-minus decay a neutron becomes a proton (plus the emitted electron), so the mass number is unchanged but the atomic number increases by 1.

questions.q: On a longitudinal wave, the wavelength is the distance between:
options: A compression and the next rarefaction
One compression and the next compression
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance for one complete wave, e.g. from one compression to the next compression (or rarefaction to rarefaction). A compression to the next rarefaction is only half a wavelength.

questions.q: Where are elements heavier than iron formed?
options: In the cores of low-mass main sequence stars
questions.explain: Fusion in stars produces elements up to iron. Elements heavier than iron are formed in the huge energies of a supernova explosion, which then scatters them into space.

questions.q: Radioactive decay is described as a random process. What does this mean?
options: Decay only happens when the source is disturbed
All nuclei decay at exactly the same time
It is impossible to predict which nucleus will decay next or when
The source decays at a steady, predictable rate per nucleus
questions.explain: Decay is random: you cannot predict which nucleus will decay or when. A Geiger–Müller tube can measure the overall count-rate, but individual decays are unpredictable.

questions.q: A blue jumper appears blue in white light because it:
options: Reflects blue light and absorbs the other colours
Absorbs blue light and reflects the rest
questions.explain: An opaque object reflects the colours we see and absorbs the others. A blue jumper reflects blue light and absorbs the remaining colours of white light.

questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used for broadcasting television and radio signals over long distances?
questions.explain: Radio waves are used for TV and radio broadcasting. They have long wavelengths and can be transmitted, received and reflected over long distances.

questions.q: A converging (convex) lens is used as a magnifying glass. Which type of image does it form when an object is very close to the lens?
options: A real image the same size
questions.explain: When an object is closer than the focal length of a convex lens, the lens produces a virtual, upright and magnified image — this is how a magnifying glass works.

questions.q: Total internal reflection is used in optical fibres. What must be true for it to occur?
options: Light must travel from a less dense to a more dense medium
The fibre must be perfectly straight
Light must travel from a more dense to a less dense medium, above the critical angle
questions.explain: For total internal reflection the light must be going from a more optically dense medium (the glass core) into a less dense one, striking the boundary above the critical angle, so it reflects rather than refracts out.

questions.q: A red book looks red in white light because it:
options: Reflects red light and absorbs the other colours
Absorbs red light and reflects all other colours
questions.explain: An opaque coloured object reflects the colours we see and absorbs the rest. A red book reflects red light and absorbs the other colours of white light.

questions.q: Which list shows the electromagnetic spectrum in order of INCREASING frequency?
options: Radio, visible, microwave, X-ray, infrared, gamma, ultraviolet
Gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Microwave, radio, infrared, visible, gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet
questions.explain: In order of increasing frequency (and decreasing wavelength): radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength.

questions.q: Within the visible spectrum, which colour has the highest frequency and shortest wavelength?
questions.explain: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and highest frequency of the visible colours, while red has the longest wavelength and lowest frequency.

questions.q: A sound wave with a frequency above 20 000 Hz is called:
questions.explain: Sound above the upper limit of human hearing (about 20 kHz) is called ultrasound. Sound below 20 Hz is infrasound.
